facts.fact: NIDA says the new digital identity system will let citizens use a digital version of their ID through a QR code on a phone or computer and a token, separate from the national ID number, to access personal information.

RWA.note: The document states no exchange between the civil register and the ID system.

facts.fact: NIDA said more than 10 million people in 27 of 30 districts have had photographs and biometrics captured, about 68% of the 14.6 million population (share computed from the population held).
NIDA said more than 10 million people have had biometrics captured, about 68% of the 14.6 million population (share computed from the population held), with 27 of 30 districts covered.

RWA.note: Children from birth to five get a photograph-only document; the document states no number at birth.
The document names a World Bank partnership but no operating or maintenance arrangement.
The document names no public register keyed on the ID number.

facts.fact: NIDA said the digital identity project, launched in 2023 with the World Bank at about Rwf200 billion, is being rolled out district by district, with biometric registration opening in Rusizi on 2026-09-16.

systems.tiers: physical card, QR digital version, token
